title: Increasing CO2 levels fertilize C4 grass production.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata for doi:10.5061/dryad.rbnzs7hq7: licence CC0-1.0, public, 1 version, 3.54 MB total. File list with sizes: Kruger_NP_vca_data.xls (3,363,840 bytes), meta_analysis_extracted_data.csv (153,154 bytes), meta_analysis_study_info.csv (16,565 bytes), meta_analysis_meta_data.txt (3,740 bytes), meta_analysis_phylogeny.tre (3,444 bytes), README.md (1,442 bytes). README text read via the landing page: the VCA (Veld Condition Assessment) file covers Kruger National Park plots 1989-2021 and has a 'variable names' tab; study_ID links the two meta-analysis CSVs. Every file download failed: the API returned 401 ('must have current bearer token') and the web file_stream links returned 403 or an Anubis proof-of-work 'Validating...' page.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about contents: 70 CO2-addition experiments, 32 years of field data, the 28% biomass increase and the 75.1 g m-2 CO2-driven gain come from the abstract. Row counts, column names, units, plot coordinates, rainfall and fire covariates, and how biomass was measured (likely a disc pasture meter calibrated to clipped biomass) are all unverified. No full text was available (paywalled, no PMCID).

a1_downloadable.note: Public under CC0 on Dryad and downloadable in a browser, but scripted download is blocked (API 401, bot challenge 403). Passed provisionally: no access application is needed, but I could not open the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Unverified. The README says the VCA file holds annual grass biomass per plot, so biomass is probably a column. The meta-analysis file probably holds per-study effect sizes. Neither was seen.

a3_inputs_present.note: Unverified. Rainfall, fire and herbivory covariates may or may not be in the xls; if they are missing, rainfall would have to be joined from CHIRPS (a gridded rainfall product) on plot coordinates and year.

a4_units_stated.note: Unverified. A 'variable names' tab and a meta-data txt exist, but I could not read them.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown. A 3.4 MB xls over 33 years is consistent with thousands of plot-years, but the independent units are plots (count unseen) and, for the meta-analysis, 70 experiments, which is small.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without the files; the only count I could confirm is the 6-file listing.

a8_label_provenance.note: The field biomass is a field measurement (likely disc pasture meter readings converted with a calibration equation), not another model's output. That is to be confirmed in the variable tab. The CLM (Community Land Model) simulations are model output and must not be used as labels.

B1.why: Two separate datasets; the meta-analysis CSVs join on study_ID, and the VCA is one xls (README only).

B2.why: Legacy .xls needs the xlrd reader; the CSVs are probably clean. Not opened.

B3.why: The VCA uses one protocol within one park; the meta-analysis effect sizes mix experiment types and need normalization.

B4.why: Unknown; missing survey years per plot are likely in a 33-year field program.

B5.why: Unknown; one meta-analysis study can report several effect sizes, so these are not independent.

B6.why: README, a meta-data txt and a variable-names tab exist, but I could not read them.

C1.why: 'Does a rainfall-plus-CO2 model transfer to held-out years?' is mixed; the CO2 effect itself is causal attribution.

C2.why: The paper's own statistical model plus remote-sensing random-forest biomass maps of Kruger exist; no ML on these plot records found.

C3.why: Weak unique-application angle: plot-level temporal forecasting of grass biomass; the paper already makes the main point.

C4.why: Annual field surveys are laborious, but a model would not replace them for management.

C5.why: Obvious dummy baselines (per-plot mean, rainfall-only regression) plus the paper's 28% / 75.1 g m-2 figures.

D1.why: No biology backbone fits; only TabPFN, a pretrained general tabular model, applies loosely.

D2.why: TabPFN-style inference runs on CPU for small tables, but it is not a true freeze-and-head setup.

D3.why: Data is CC0; TabPFN's licence carries attribution terms.

E1.why: Hold out whole plots or later years; the 1989-2021 span is stated in the README.

E2.why: Likely many plots across Kruger, but the plot count is unverified.

E3.why: Per-plot mean and rainfall-only regression are trivial to compute.

E4.why: No replicate biomass measurements per plot-year are known.

E5.why: The textbook rainfall-biomass relationship in savannas must be recovered.

E6.why: Shuffle labels within year; ablate the CO2/year term.

E7.why: Year column enables a temporal split; MODIS satellite productivity is an independent check.

E8.why: Could reproduce the paper's 28% three-decade increase from the VCA file, once it can be opened.

G1.why: Plot coordinates are probably present (unverified); the meta-analysis uses species names plus a phylogeny tree.

G2.why: CHIRPS rainfall or MODIS productivity, joinable on coordinates and year, is plausible.

G3.why: One plot-year to one grid cell-year is manageable; the grid scale is coarser than the plots.

G4.why: Joining satellite data would test whether satellites see the CO2 signal; marginally new.

H1.why: The label is continuous; the meta-analysis presumably includes null CO2 responses (unverified).

H2.why: Field data comes from one park in one country; the meta-analysis spans 70 experiments.

H3.why: The claim is stated precisely below.

H4.why: The single-park limit is obvious; how plots were sampled is not visible without the files.

I1.why: SANParks (South African National Parks) scientists and savanna carbon modellers, loosely.

I2.why: Fuel-load forecasts could inform fire planning, but only marginally.

I3.why: RMSE (prediction error) on held-out years roughly matches a fuel-load forecast.

I4.why: A mixed-effects regression on rainfall, fire and year likely matches ML.

J1.why: Small-data tabular modelling with temporal splits; no transfer learning.

J2.why: Ecology intuition is needed to judge biomass values; rainfall sanity checks help.

J3.why: A reproduced trend plus a temporal-split benchmark is shareable.

J4.why: One to two weekends, not formally set.

J5.why: Kill rule below; not yet written in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: The paper's own statistical analysis of the VCA plots and CLM (Community Land Model) simulations
existing_models.score_and_split: Reports a 28% increase and a CO2-driven 75.1 g m-2 (95% CI 74.5-75.8); no predictive split reported in the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The fate of the extra carbon depends on feedbacks with fire, herbivory and woody vegetation (abstract).

existing_models.name: Random-forest annual grass biomass mapping from Landsat-8 and Sentinel-2 over Kruger (IEEE IGARSS 2020; search result title and snippet only)
XGBoost on Sentinel-1 radar features for grass carbon stock in Kruger (Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences, 2024; search result only)

backbone.name: None from biology; TabPFN (a pretrained tabular model) at most
backbone.licence: Data CC0-1.0; TabPFN uses its own licence with attribution terms

integration.partner_dataset: CHIRPS daily rainfall and MODIS MOD17 net primary productivity (satellite-derived)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is the CO2-driven rise in grass production seen on Kruger plots also visible in satellite productivity across all southern African savannas?

controls.positive_control: Recover the known positive rainfall-biomass relationship; reproduce the paper's 28% three-decade increase.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle biomass within year; drop the year/CO2 term and confirm the trend residual appears.
controls.external_validation: Temporal hold-out (e.g. 2015-2021) and MODIS productivity for the same pixels.

honest_claim_h3: Within Kruger National Park's monitored plots, 1989-2021, the model predicts annual grass biomass on held-out years from rainfall, fire history and the year/CO2 trend; it cannot separate CO2 from other slow trends such as changing grazing.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use rainfall, fire history and year to predict each plot's annual grass growth in Kruger Park, testing on later years.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per field plot per survey year, with rainfall, fire and herbivore context; the number of rows is unknown because the file could not be opened.
plain_idea.predict: Grass dry biomass per square metre in that plot that year, as measured in Kruger's annual Veld Condition Assessment field survey.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Park managers plan burns on grass fuel loads; a forecast that holds up on later years would show whether the CO2 trend helps prediction beyond rainfall.

more_or_better_data.why: 33 years of ground-measured plot biomass is far longer than the 2016-2018 satellite training sets, but the row count is unverified.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements per plot-year are known, so per-prediction noise cannot be estimated from the data.

models_beatable.why: The satellite random-forest models predict a different target (maps, not plot time series); the paper's regression is the real baseline and is likely hard to beat.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing predictive model on this split is runnable as a baseline, and the added satellite data measures something different.

label_elsewhere.sources: Other savanna long-term plots (e.g. Serengeti) and elevated-CO2 experiment databases exist (known resources, not searched); MODIS productivity is a model product, not a measured label.
label_elsewhere.join_key: Coordinates + year; species names for the meta-analysis
label_elsewhere.why: A second park's plot biomass would allow a cross-site transfer test, but those records are scattered and hard to join.

risks: The same plot appears in both training and test years, so the model memorizes plot identity.
A shared rainfall year links all plots, so a random split leaks year effects.
Several effect sizes from one meta-analysis study land on both sides of the split.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out the final years (e.g. 2015-2021) and separately hold out whole plots; the meta-analysis groups by study_ID. None of these columns was seen in the files.
checks: Shuffle biomass within year and confirm the score falls to the per-plot mean.
Fit on plot ID alone to measure how much is identity memorization.
Compare the temporal-split and random-split scores; a large gap means leakage.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable if splits are by year and plot.

success_criteria.metric: RMSE (root mean squared error) of biomass in g m-2 on held-out later years, which matches a fuel-load forecast.
success_criteria.baselines: Per-plot mean and a rainfall-only linear model; no number exists yet (data unopened).
success_criteria.success: At least 15% lower RMSE than the rainfall-only model on 2015-2021 (a threshold chosen in advance, not from the data).
success_criteria.kill: If the files can't be opened manually, or the plot count is under 100, stop.

ambitious.why: It publishes CO2-vegetation analyses, but would need the satellite extension to show the signal region-wide.

realistic.why: It takes ecological forecasting benchmarks with honest temporal splits on long-term monitoring data.

fallback.why: A reproduction and forecast note is worth posting even if ML adds nothing over regression.

pitch.headline: 33 years (1989-2021) of field-measured grass biomass from Kruger plots, CC0, 3.5 MB in total.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Ground-measured savanna grass production over three decades is rare; satellite models train on 2-3 years. Contents rest on the README and abstract only; I opened no files.
pitch.the_win: A forecast that beats a rainfall-only model by at least 15% RMSE on held-out years 2015-2021.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn whether the year/CO2 trend adds predictive power beyond rainfall; a null result is a short note, not a paper.
pitch.who_wants_it: SANParks scientific services planning fire on fuel loads; the Staver (Princeton) and Simpson (Sheffield) groups.

ml_idea: Temporal-split regression of plot-year grass biomass on rainfall, fire and the year/CO2 trend, compared with rainfall-only and per-plot baselines; optionally join CHIRPS and MODIS on coordinates.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 3.5 MB total file size in the Dryad metadata; nothing timed because no file could be downloaded.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download Kruger_NP_vca_data.xls in a browser and count distinct plots and plot-years with non-missing biomass; check whether rainfall and coordinates are columns.

verdict_reason: No files could be opened: Dryad's API needs a login token and its download links serve a bot check, so every Part A check rests on the README. Even if the files are clean, no pretrained model fits and plain regression likely matches ML on a one-park question that is about causes.
